rawFindings.title: Loss of handling for multiple occurrences of same argument
rawFindings.explanation: Previously, when an argument was provided multiple times (which optimist parses as an array), the code would take the last value by popping the array to get a single string value. This change removes that logic and directly assigns argv[name] (which may be an array) to options[...], potentially overwriting the expected single value with an array.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore handling of multiple argument instances by checking if argv[name] is an array and, if so, use the last element (pop) as the final value to assign to options.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When the CLI is called with multiple instances of the same argument, such as '--port 123 --port 456', options.port will be set as [123, 456] instead of the expected '456'. This could cause unexpected behavior in code expecting options.port to be a single value.
